newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up at close on month-end demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up at close on month-end demand.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed firmer Friday on normal month-end demand, but volume remained slim as U.S. dealers stayed away after Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday.

"Although the market sleepwalked for most of the session with the lack of foreign dealers slowing things down, month-end demand picked prices up towards the close," said Esteban Rojas, deputy research director at Arka brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 18.60 points, or 0.57 percent, at 3,291.69. Volume was lifeless at 39.9 million shares traded
Stability in the foreign exchange and money markets also bolstered the bourse, analysts said.
"Although the market has yet to react favourably to macroeconomic data because of political unease, I feel the other markets helped stock prices," Rojas added.
On the broad market, a total of 109 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 51 to 29.

Simec, the steelmaking arm of the debt-ridden Sidek group, topped the gainers' list, up 12 centavos (2 cents) at 1.48 pesos (19 cents). Traders said the movement was technical, and noted the stock was well below its year high of 2.96 pesos (38 cents).
Food companies Herdez and Maizoro headed the losers, down 13 centavos (2 cents) and 9 centavos (1 cent), respectively, at 2.41 pesos (31 cents) and 2.61 pesos (33 cents).
Traders said they expected trading volume to pick up next week and for stocks to gain more steadily, unless the Dow Jones were to suffer a bout of profit-taking.
The IPC closed the month up 129.20 points from the end of October, or 4.09 percent.
